q: 1. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distance directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescope alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured tacheometrically directly during plane tabling, without chaining.

q: 2. The operation of revolving a plane table about its vertical axis so that all lines on the sheet become parallel to corresponding lines on the ground, is known
explain: Orientation is the process of rotating the plane table so that all lines on the plotted sheet remain parallel to their corresponding lines on the ground.

q: 3. In setting up a plane table at any station
options: both leveling and centering are done simultaneously
explain: When setting up a plane table, leveling and centering are carried out together (simultaneously) as adjustments to one affect the other.

q: 4. Pick up the method of surveying in which field observations and plotting proceed simultaneously from the following
explain: Plane table surveying is unique in that field observation and plotting are carried out together at the same time in the field.

q: 5. Which one of the following procedures for getting accurate orientation is the most distinctive feature of the art of plane tabling
explain: Resection (particularly the two-point and three-point problems) is considered the most distinctive and skill-demanding feature of plane table surveying, used to orient the table accurately.

q: 6. The angle of intersection of the horizon glass and index glass in an optical square is
explain: In an optical square, the two mirrors (horizon glass and index glass) are fixed at 45 degrees to each other, causing the incident ray to be deflected through 90 degrees via double reflection.

q: 7. Methods adopted for traversing are
options: chain traversing and loose needle method
chain angle method and fast needle method
explain: Traversing can be done using various methods such as 'loose needle' (compass), 'fast needle' (theodolite), or by measuring angles between lines using a chain.

q: 8. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Points that are inaccessible (cannot be reached to measure distance) but are visible from two known plane table stations are plotted using the intersection method.

q: 9. The process of putting the plane table into some fixed position so that a line representing certain direction of the plane is parallel to the direction in the field is known as
explain: Orientation is the process of aligning the plane table so that lines drawn on the sheet are parallel to the corresponding lines/directions on the ground.

q: 10. In the method of plane table survey the object to be plotted is sighted from two plane table stations. This method is called as
explain: Sighting the same object from two different, known plane table stations and plotting its position at the intersection of the two resulting rays is the method of intersection.

q: 11. The traversing by the method of deflection angles is chiefly used in
explain: The deflection angle method of traversing is commonly used across all types of linear engineering works - canals, highways, and railways - since it directly gives the angle by which the alignment changes at each station.

q: 12. The distances AC and BC are measured from two fixed points A and B whose distance AB is known. The point C is plotted by intersection. This method is generally adopted in
explain: Locating an unknown point C by measuring/computing angles or distances from two known points A and B on a fixed baseline, and plotting by intersection, is the basic principle of triangulation.

q: 13. The plane table surveying is
options: most suitable for preparing small-scale maps
less costly than a theodolite survey
explain: Plane table surveying is well suited for small-scale mapping, is unaffected by local magnetic attraction (unlike compass surveys), and is generally less costly than theodolite surveying, so all the listed statements are true.

q: 14. The method of intersection in plane tabling is commonly used for
options: locating the distant and inaccessible points
locating the points which may be used subsequently as the instrument stations
explain: Intersection is a versatile method used to locate distant/inaccessible points, broken boundary details, and even future instrument stations, so all the listed uses apply.

q: 15. An advantage of plane tabling is
options: changes to miss details are less
explain: A key advantage of plane tabling is that plotting is done outdoors in the field itself, alongside the observations, reducing the chance of errors from later office plotting.

q: 16. Plane table survey is considered good as compared to other survey since
options: chances to missing details are less
explain: Since plotting happens while looking at the actual terrain, the surveyor is much less likely to omit important features.

q: 17. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table used in surveying is typically about 600 mm x 750 mm in size, as given by this text.

q: 18. The type of surveying which requires least office work is
explain: Since plotting is done directly in the field alongside observation in plane table surveying, it requires the least amount of subsequent office (indoor) computation and plotting work.

q: 19. The process of aligning the plane table by rotating it in the horizontal plane to the corresponding lines on the ground
explain: Rotation to align with ground features is the definition of orientation.

q: 20. In case of resection method of plane table, the relation between great triangle and great circle are
options: the area of great triangle is more than great circle
the area of great triangle is less than great circle
the area of great triangle is equal to great circle
explain: Geometrically, the circle passing through the three points (great circle) encloses the triangle (great triangle).

q: 21. The fix of table is good when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the middle station is much nearer than other two stations
the angle subtended between two stations is not very small
explain: A good fix requires geometry that avoids 'danger circles' where the position becomes indeterminate.

q: 22. A poor fix of the table is
options: when station is within the great triangle
when station is near the great circle
explain: If the instrument station lies on or near the circle passing through the three known points, the solution becomes unreliable.

q: 23. The two point problem and three point problems are methods of
explain: Both problems solve for the station's location and the table's orientation simultaneously.

q: 24. The resection by two point problem as compared to the three point problem
explain: Two-point resection is more cumbersome and usually less accurate than three-point resection.

q: 25. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
explain: Intersection is preferred in hills where measuring horizontal distance on steep slopes is difficult.

q: 26. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: As stated in Q104, this technique of plotting all accessible points from a single plane table setup is called radiation.

q: 27. The 'fix' of a plane table station with three known points, is bad if the plane station lies
options: on the circumference of the circumscribing circle
explain: The three-point problem 'fix' is considered bad (unreliable/indeterminate) specifically when the plane table station lies on the circumference of the circle passing through the three known points, since the solution becomes indeterminate there.

q: 28. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted, is
explain: When orienting a plane table at a station using only two known but inaccessible points, the specific technique used is the two-point problem, a form of resection using two references.

q: 29. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest divisions of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of divisions of vernier scale
value of one division of vernier scale divided by total number of divisions of primary scale
explain: The least count of a vernier is defined as the value of one division of the main (primary) scale divided by the total number of divisions on the vernier scale.

q: 30. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: it is heavy, cumbersome and awkward to carry
it cannot be used in wet climate
details may not be available while redrawing to a different scale
accessories are likely to be lost
explain: A significant practical disadvantage of plane table surveying is that the table and its equipment are heavy, cumbersome, and awkward to carry, especially over rough terrain.

q: 31. The operation of turning the table so that all the lines on the paper are parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground is called
explain: This operation of rotating the plane table so plotted lines remain parallel to corresponding ground lines is, by definition, orientation.

q: 32. If the plane table is not horizontal in a direction at right angles to the alidade, the line of sight is parallel to the fiducial edge only for
explain: When the plane table is not perfectly horizontal, the line of sight through the alidade remains parallel to its fiducial (ruling) edge only for purely horizontal sights; inclined sights introduce an error under these conditions.
